A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Logicbreaks by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material that was relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v2 reports original learned-reasoner experiments, GPT-2 attack and probing results on Minecraft tasks, and Llama-2 attention analyses in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Llama-3 attention results and an analysis comparing strict and simpler attack-success criteria.

M1.justification: The rule-suppression attack changes from the modified antecedent ζ = α − κ(1 − α) in v2 to an (α, −β) cancellation token in v3, including its repeated form in Appendix C.3. Theorem 3.4 also introduces an attention-suppression adaptation. This materially revises one of the three central attacks, while retaining the Horn-logic reasoner and learned-attack objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic Horn-rule data, Minecraft crafting tasks and depth settings, proposition-restricted probing datasets, and 15 custom topic queries. Adding Llama-3 changes the evaluated model, not the represented data or task coverage.

E2.justification: No competing attack method is added or removed. GCG, its universal multi-prompt variant, learned suffix optimization, and manual suffix tests remain. Llama-3 is an additional attacked model, not a new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: v3 adds Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct to the manual rule-suppression evaluation and introduces a simpler ASR criterion counting any incorrect output alongside exact target matching in Figure 8. Existing dataset splits, training budgets, and sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 and Appendix C.4 examine whether nonmonotonic attack success as suffix repetitions increase depends on the success criterion. They compare retained strict-ASR curves with new simple-ASR curves. Figure 13 documents the existing attention example rather than establishing a separate new case study.

E5.justification: The five-seed median reporting in Figure 7 and the uncertainty-reporting practices in Tables 1–3 are retained. Changed uncertainty values in Table 1 do not establish a changed estimation procedure, and no new significance tests or run-count requirements are reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all four targeted-entry magnitude estimates; for n = 64, 0.01 ± 0.001 becomes 0.77 ± 0.07. This reverses their ordering relative to non-targeted entries and changes important evidence for the proposed mechanism, while ASRs remain unchanged. v3 also adds Llama-3 attention measurements and simple-ASR curves. Tables 2–4 and the relocated Llama-2 results retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: v3 adds Theorem 3.4 and its proof under a nonsingular attention-block assumption, and revises the maximality-attack construction and reasoning in Theorems 3.3 and B.9. The MMS characterization and sparse-reasoner construction remain. The explicit autoregressive equation added to the main text already appeared in v2 Appendix B.2.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its rule-following expressivity statement from LLMs to small transformers. The introduction explicitly qualifies the connection to LLM behavior as preliminary and empirical. The principal contributions—Horn-logic characterization, transferable attacks, and alignment with automated jailbreak behavior—remain.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes cancellation in the constructed reasoner from attention suppression in learned models and explains nonmonotonic strict ASR through the evaluation criterion. It adds cautions about interpreting attention-layer importance and drawing definitive LLM conclusions from small-model theory. The conclusion replaces its positional-encoding limitation with the empirical-only connection, while retaining the logic and safety-training scope limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 clarifies that overlap concerns successful attacks and specifies tokenizer-level salient tokens, including exclusions of non-item words. Figure 13 supplies the full prompt, suffix, and generations underlying an existing attention visualization. Core hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and code/data source links remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Brody et al. on layer normalization and the Llama-3 model card. It sharpens the distinction from Zhang et al. around adversarial violations of in-distribution rules and adds an explicit early-contribution positioning statement. The broader related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: Several passages are rewritten or expanded, especially the abstract, contribution statements, transformer encoding explanation, related work, and conclusion. GCG receives more explanation in the main text, and probing moves from the first to the last result in Section 4. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the four-panel Figure 8 and the detailed example in Figure 13. It introduces a Llama-3 Table 5 while moving the original Llama-2 table to Appendix D.4 as Table 6. The probing figure is relocated and renumbered, and several captions expand; most existing graphics and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves internal consistency and transparency: Table 1 now supports its stated magnitude ordering, Figure 8 explains metric sensitivity, and Llama-3 results and clearer caveats strengthen the empirical presentation. Theoretical repair remains incomplete: revised Theorem B.9 retains incompatible premises, since an applicable rule already implies β ⊆ Apply[Γ](Φ), contrary to its required nonempty difference. The additions therefore support a limited overall improvement.
